name: English
metaTitle: HUMAN-INTENT.md — the file that keeps AI coding under human control
metaDescription: HUMAN-INTENT.md is a single file, written only by a human, that acts as law for AI agents: the project's architecture, development rules, and product decisions.
tagline: One file. Written by a human. Law for agents.
problem: We don't want to read code anymore. We don't want to watch over agents or track every detail.
But without control, agents turn any project into chaos. It's only a matter of time.
idea: HUMAN-INTENT.md is one file in the root of your repository. It holds your intent: architecture, rules, product.
It's not documentation. It's law for the code.

rules.title: Only you write it
rules.body: Agents don't touch this file. Every line is a human decision.

rules.title: For the agent, it's law
rules.body: The file outranks everything. If the code contradicts it, the code is wrong.

rules.title: Intent, not recipes
rules.body: The agent knows every pattern. You state what must be true — and why.

why: A new agent session remembers nothing. The file gives the context back — so the hundredth session follows the same principles as the first.
You steer development without reading code. And the project's principles never erode.
how: Create HUMAN-INTENT.md in the root of your repository.
Write down the decisions you've made: architecture, rules, product.
Tell your agent it's law — point to it from AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md.
New decision — new line in the file.
Review the file, not the code.
